text:
Maya: starting a small canary for the new rate-cap smoothing change. details: reduce burst window from 60s -> 30s and soft per-key cap 600->400 req/min. canary id rc-canary-042, rollout 5% traffic in us-west1. kicking off at 2026-03-15T10:00Z. posting here for watchers and to lock rollback triggers.
Tom: noted. what SLIs are we guarding? p95 latency, 5xx rate, and 429 rate? where can I watch the dashboards (link pls).
Maya: yep p95 latency and 429 spikes are primary. dashboard: https://console.redwood.internal/dashboards/rc-canary-042 (read-only link). Grafana panels: token-throughput, per-key-429s, p95-latency-by-region. i'll paste a short checklist below.
Priya: support seeing a handful of live customer reports. 3 distinct orgs opened tickets in the last hour complaining about unexpected 429s. i pulled a quick repro from one customer (sanitized):

```bash
# reproducer curl from customer:
curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-cust-xxx' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"input":"hello"}' \
  'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate'
```

Response snippet they pasted back:

HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
X-RateLimit-Limit: 400
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
Retry-After: 30

{ "error": "rate_limit_exceeded", "detail": "burst capacity exceeded" }

Priya: they said this started right around 10:12 UTC (2x requests per second burst for ~20s). i've escalated and asked for request ids. i'll add them here when they arrive.
deploy-bot: [deploy] rc-canary-042 started at 2026-03-15T10:00Z, region=us-west1, traffic=5% (hash-based routing). commit=b6a3f9d

Tom: thanks. small ask: can support paste the request-ids (x-request-id) so we can trace kv-cache state and shard assignment. also i'm going to tail the ingress logs with grep for the canary token pattern: 

```bash
# tail ingress where canary tag present
kubectl -n ingress logs -f --since=15m | grep rc-canary-042 | grep 429
```

Priya: pasted two request ids: req_44a1, req_44a2. both from same org.

Tom: traced req_44a1 -> edge node e-12 -> runtime pod r-77 -> saw quota check fail at rate_limiter.go:142. attaching small log lines:

```
2026-03-15T10:12:05Z INFO rate_limiter.go:142 key=org-99 burst_count=21 limit=400 window=30s result=reject
2026-03-15T10:12:06Z WARN proxy.go:88 upstream=runtime-77 status=429 x-request-id=req_44a1
```

Alex: are we sure the change from 60s->30s is the right knob for this workload? a couple of our customer apps do periodic short bursts and will be affected. product note: we expected ~5% of customers to see transient 429s at 5% canary but not persistent ones.

Maya: agreed. that's why we kept it at 5% and want tight rollback triggers. proposing rollback criteria (if any are met, immediate rollback to previous rate policy):
- >=5 unique customers returning 429s within a 15-minute window
- sustained p95 latency regression > 30% over baseline for canary group for 10m
- any business-critical customer (tier=enterprise) reports repeat failures and requests rollback

Tom: add one more: spike in downstream auth failures or 5xxs correlated with rate changes (suggest threshold: 0.5% absolute increase in 5xx across canary for 10m).

Priya: support wants an automated alert too. i can add a PagerDuty rule if we can surface a metric: metric name: canary.ratecap.429_count_by_org in prometheus. trigger: >=5 distinct orgs in 15m. i can wire that up now.

Maya: please do. i'll also open a temporary runbook in confluence and pin here. quick checklist for watchers:
1) watch canary dashboard for 15m after rollout
2) collect request ids for any 429s and post here
3) support to create PD alert for distinct-org-429s
4) eng-sre to tail ingress/runtime logs and be ready to rollback
5) product to coordinate if enterprise customer impacted

Alex: if we need to rollback, what's the rollback plan (ops steps)?

Tom: rollback is one-line via infra pipeline: set rate-policy to previous commit b6a3f9d -> b5d2c1a and re-deploy config. i can execute and validate in ~2-3 mins, then escalate to 25% holdback for 10m before full restoration. will post deploy-bot confirmation.

Maya: timeline: 10:00 canary start. check 10:00-10:30. if stable, ramp to 10% at 10:30 (manual). otherwise rollback immediately. Priya and Tom, owners for first 30m watches. Alex will own customer comms.

Priya: wiring PD alert now, will update with policy name. also prepping message templates for customers (short apology, mitigation steps, ETA).

Tom: i'm currently seeing 429s at ingress at 10:12-10:14 but volume modest (2 orgs). i'll keep tailing and post counts every 5m.

Maya: thanks. one more small test step for eng-platform/devs: please run a synthetic burst against the canary bucket to validate eviction behavior. use canary header x-canary-id: rc-canary-042 to route test traffic.

Tom: running a quick loadgen (10s burst, 5 req/s) with header. results: 12/50 requests got 429s, matched the policy cap. no downstream 5xx.

Priya: customer req ids now: req_44a1, req_44a2, req_44b7. adding to ticket.

Maya: ACTIONS:
- Priya: PD alert and customer templates (owner)
- Tom: be ready to rollback and collect logs (owner)
- Alex: monitor enterprise tickets and own comms (owner)
- Maya: runbook + gate decisions, will execute ramp/rollback (owner)

Maya: i'll post status updates here. if you see numbers hitting rollback triggers, call it out with the word "ROLLBACK" so i don't miss it. :rotating_light:

(30m later)

Tom: status update 10:40Z — canary p95 latency +10% vs baseline, 429s in 15m window from 4 distinct orgs, largest org is mid-tier. counts trending up. recommending rollback now.

Priya: support: 2 enterprise customers pinged CS and asked for mitigation. they haven't escalated contract breach yet but affected workflows.

Maya: ROLLBACK. executing rollback to previous rate-policy now.

deploy-bot: [deploy] rollback-start rc-canary-042 -> policy=b5d2c1a at 2026-03-15T10:41Z

Tom: rollback applied. validating...

deploy-bot: [deploy] rollback-done policy=b5d2c1a at 2026-03-15T10:43Z

Tom: post-rollback check: 10:50Z p95 back within baseline, 429s dropped to pre-canary levels. no 5xx increase observed.

Priya: customer comms sent to impacted orgs with apology and note that change was rolled back. PD alert closed.

Maya: thanks everyone. lessons: 1) need a smaller short-burst exemption for certain clients or a staged policy per-tier; 2) consider increasing canary observability for distinct-org metrics. i'll schedule a follow-up tomorrow to capture policy alternatives. :white_check_mark:
